title: Wanting Does Nothing
logline: In a belt of crowded home gardens behind the west coast, three men spend a morning reading one big garden tree — its lean, the weight in its crown, the rot at its foot, and the few metres it has to fall into between a house wall, a well head and a line of wire — and then in about two seconds the tree goes where they cut it to go, and nothing after that can be corrected.
human_question: If everything a person can do arrives in the two seconds it takes, what were all the years before it for?

place.what_kind_of_place: An inland belt of the wet-zone lowlands a few hours behind the coast, where there is no line anywhere between garden, village and forest. Seen from the air it is one continuous canopy with roofs under it: coconut, jak, mango, breadfruit, areca, rambutan, and in most gardens two or three big timber trees that were planted or left standing by somebody's grandparents. Almost all the sawn timber the country uses comes out of ground like this rather than out of forest, and jak is one of the three species that produce most of it. The working unit is tiny and entirely local: a gang of three, a chainsaw and a hand file, a bush knife, an axe, a jack, a coil of rope, and wedges split out of the last tree they took down; behind them a lorry on the lane and, a few kilometres away, a small sawmill with a stack of boards under a tin roof and a yard of sawdust. The gardens are crowded in a way that matters to the work. A tree twenty-two metres tall often has an opening only a little wider than that to fall into, and the things at the edge of the opening are a tiled roof, a well, a cattle shed, a boundary wall, a young coconut somebody is counting on, and the wire that feeds four houses.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because the place produces one image that is also the whole idea. From height, before the work, the canopy is unbroken except for a single crown of a different green standing clear above it. From height the next morning, there is a hole in the canopy and a rectangle of sun lying on ground that has been in shade for fifty years, with a well and the edge of a roof at the margin of it. The difference between those two frames is the film, and the difference took about two seconds. Everything else in the morning is approach, and the approach is the part that rewards close filming: a walk round the foot; an axe head tapped against a root buttress and a head turned to listen; a string with a nut tied to it held up and sighted against the trunk; the gap paced out twice; the crown looked at for a long time and from three positions; a chain filed tooth by tooth on the lorry's tailgate; a rope thrown over a limb on the third attempt. Then a scarf cut, checked with a flat hand laid inside it, and a stop. Then one back-cut, one wedge, two taps.
place.what_moves_or_changes: Nothing for three hours and then everything at once, one time only. The tree cannot be test-dropped, the cut cannot be undone, and the gang will not do it twice for a camera because there is only one tree. After the fall the place changes at ordinary speed and in a completely unremarkable way: limbs lopped, the trunk cross-cut and rolled with a pole, chalk marks, a wet cut face, the smell of sap, sawdust, a lorry loaded, somebody eating. Over a longer clock the garden closes the gap again within a few seasons, and the gang is in another garden the same afternoon. Nothing about the day is exceptional to the people doing it; it is the third or fourth tree of the week and about the four-hundredth of a working life.
place.when_it_looks_best: Dry weather, because nothing is felled in wind or on wet ground, and because the aerial work needs still air. Within a day, the canopy and the gap want the first and the last hour, when the crowns separate from one another and the lanes and roofs come out from under them. The fall itself cannot be given to the light: it happens when the cuts are finished, usually in flat mid-morning, and the film has to take it as it comes. The single most valuable return visit is the following morning, for the new light on the cleared ground, and that has to be planned for in advance because by the afternoon the trunk is gone.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A film about one tree coming down in a crowded garden. A canopy at first light with a single crown above it; three men arriving on a lane; an axe tapped against a root; a string held up against a trunk; a gap paced out between a well and a wall; a chain filed on a tailgate; a rope thrown; a scarf cut and checked with a hand; everybody moved to one side; a back-cut, a wedge, two taps, and a whole fall held in one shot to the end with the ground jumping once. Then a long moment in which nobody says anything, and then the completely ordinary rest of it: lopping, cross-cutting, rolling, loading, boards stacked under a tin roof. It has a full shape with nothing said over it, and anyone who likes exact work, or big trees, or the small distance between a roof and twenty metres of falling timber, has a whole piece here.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same morning becomes the sources' own list of ten kinds of accomplishment, and their own ranking of what is hard. The list opens with the largest claims the tradition makes and closes with a person who ploughs and sows properly, and the word underneath all ten turns out to be nothing more mysterious than this: what somebody meant to bring about actually comes about. The texts are then blunt about how the first three kinds are reached — deep absorption first, then a separate training for each, graduated coarse before fine and near before far, with the mind taken through the same states in every direction until it is workable — and blunter still that wanting a thing achieves nothing. And they put at the top of their ladder not a feat but instant stillness in the face of somebody else's sudden danger. The voice never says the gang has any of this. It says the opposite out loud: nobody here is in danger, nobody here is doing what the texts describe, and the film is neither asserting nor setting out to disprove that anybody anywhere does. What the morning can carry is the proportion — years of repetition, two seconds of result, and no way to want the years shorter.

sequence.on_screen: First light, high and slow over a mosaic of home gardens. Coconut, jak, mango, roofs, lanes, a cattle shed, no boundary visible anywhere between garden and village. In the middle of the frame one crown of a different green, standing clear above everything around it. Nothing is moving.
sequence.voice: The book this film is built on keeps a list of ten kinds of power, and the list is arranged in a way nobody expects. It opens with the largest claims a tradition can make — one person becoming many, passing through a wall, reaching the moon with a hand. It closes with a farmer who ploughs and sows properly, a student who learns, a healer who treats, a craftsman who has got a trade right [C090-P4:L121–L127]. The word underneath all ten is not magic. It is that what somebody meant to bring about actually comes about [C090-P4:L24].

sequence.on_screen: Three men in the garden. A walk round the foot of the tree. An axe head tapped against a root buttress, and a head turned to listen to it. A string with a nut tied on the end held up at arm's length and sighted against the trunk. The opening paced out twice: a tiled roof, a well head, a boundary wall, a line of wire. The crown looked at for a long time, from three different positions.
sequence.voice: None of this is that list's first three kinds. Those, the sources say, come only to somebody who has already mastered the deepest absorptions and then trained again, separately, for each one; and they are blunt that merely thinking a thing or saying it should happen achieves nothing at all [C089-M:L25; C090-P:L25–L46]. What is happening in this garden is the last kind on the list and no other: correct method, patiently applied, by people who have done it before.

sequence.on_screen: The ordinary repetitions, close and without commentary. A chain filed tooth by tooth on the lorry's tailgate. Wedges split out of a piece of the last tree. A rope coiled and thrown over a limb on the third attempt. A younger man's scarf cut opened up and re-cut by the older one without a word passing. Then three grey, flat stumps in three other gardens, from earlier weeks.
sequence.voice: The training the texts describe for the rare abilities is not a talent and not a moment. It is slow and graduated, coarse before fine and near before far, and before anything can be built on a settled mind that mind has to be taken through the same states in every direction: forwards, backwards, skipping, changing what it rests on while holding the state, changing the state while holding what it rests on [C101-P:L87–L102]. The pictures the source chooses for this are a goldsmith heating gold again and again and a potter kneading clay [C089-P4:L118]. The material has to become workable before anything at all can be made out of it.

sequence.on_screen: The last quarter of an hour. The scarf finished and checked with a flat hand laid inside it. Everybody moved to one side and standing still. The back-cut begun, the saw taken out, a wedge tapped twice. Then the crown moving — the whole fall in one shot, held to the end, the ground jumping once. Dust in the light. Then nothing at all, for a long moment.
sequence.voice: In the sources' own account of how one of these knowledges actually arrives, almost the whole of it is approach. Settle deeply; come out; state plainly what is intended; settle again; come out again — and then, after three or four perfectly ordinary moments of mind, one single moment is the thing itself [C101-P:L45–L48; C101-M:L5]. The proportion is the part worth noticing. Everything is preparation except the part that is not.

sequence.on_screen: The stillness afterwards. The three men standing where they moved to, doing nothing, looking at the tree on the ground. The house wall a couple of metres from the outermost branch. A hen walking out from under a veranda. Somebody's hand still on a rope that is no longer holding anything.
sequence.voice: The sources also rank the difficulties, and their ranking is not the one anybody would guess. Each rung, they say, is reached by one in a very great many [C089-P4:L98], and at the top of the list is not a feat that anybody could watch. It is being able to become still instantly, so as to act calmly the moment somebody else is suddenly in danger [C089-P4:L104–L108]. So this film has to say plainly what it is not. Nobody was in danger here. Nobody has been rescued. Nobody in this garden has anything the texts are describing, and the film neither claims that of anybody nor sets out to disprove it of anybody.

sequence.on_screen: The aftermath at working speed, without music. Limbs lopped and thrown into a heap. The trunk cross-cut, rolled with a pole, chalk-marked. A wet cut face with sap standing on it. Sawdust in the grass. The lorry loaded. Somebody sitting on the log, eating.
sequence.voice: Only one of the ten kinds is said to belong to fully freed people alone, and it is not a feat either. It is being able to meet something repulsive without recoiling, something alluring without being pulled in, and both of them with the same steadiness [C090-P4:L85–L87; C090-M:L13]. In the source that steadiness is reached through goodwill; it is not coldness, and it is not anything visible on three tired faces. And one thing the sources' own stories must never be turned into: a promise that calm or decent people are kept safe. A tree does not know who is standing under it, and the film does not pretend otherwise.

sequence.on_screen: Last light the following day, from height. The canopy with a hole in it, and a rectangle of sun lying on ground that has been in shade for fifty years, with the well and the edge of the roof at the margin. Then, at ground level, boards stacked and stickered under a tin roof, and the yard going dark.
sequence.voice: The sources are not finally impressed by any of it. They call these powers worldly, useful as a support and nothing more, and they tell the practitioner not to be satisfied with them but to turn towards understanding how suffering works and how it stops [C089-P4:L26; C101-P4:L134]. What a morning like this one can show is only a shape: that a capacity is made out of repetition across years, that it does the whole of its work in about two seconds, and that wanting it does nothing to build it. The rest is light arriving on ground that has not had any.

concept_merge.why_together: C089 supplies the ranking and the refusal. It states that deep calm does not by itself produce any of these abilities, that each one needs its own separate preparation after the base absorption is mastered [C089-P4:L98], that mere thinking or saying achieves nothing [C089-M:L25], that the images for making a mind workable are a goldsmith's gold and a potter's clay [C089-P4:L118], that the hardest and rarest use of any of it is instant stillness for the sake of somebody else in sudden danger [C089-P4:L104–L108], and that the powers are worldly and a support for wisdom rather than a substitute for it [C089-P4:L26]. C101 supplies the proportion, which is what makes this a film rather than a lecture: the same seven knowledges described as a process, in which the approach is long and the result is one single mind-moment arriving after three or four perfectly ordinary ones [C101-P:L45–L48; C101-M:L5], with the training itself set out as graduated work in fourteen directions [C101-P:L87–L102] and with the whole thing ranked below insight and warned against [C101-P4:L134]. C090 supplies the frame that keeps the film honest at both ends: a list of ten kinds of accomplishment whose last member is explicitly a craft, a treatment, a study, a ploughing and a sowing done right [C090-P4:L121–L127], whose underlying word is simply the bringing about of what was intended [C090-P4:L24], whose one item reserved for the fully freed is an even response to the repulsive and the alluring rather than any feat [C090-P4:L85–L87; C090-M:L13], and whose protection stories the digest forbids turning into a promise of safety. A garden felling is the tenth item on that list and nothing else, and it is the only place in the group where a long-built capacity can be watched discharging completely inside two seconds without anybody being in danger.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That the tradition's own ordering of power puts patient method at the bottom of nothing — it puts it in the same list as the miracles — and puts instant, invisible readiness above every spectacle. Stated flat, that is an interesting sentence. Put on a morning in which three men spend three hours on approach and two seconds on result, it becomes a measurable proportion that the viewer feels before the voice names it. The film also gets the concept's hardest guard for nothing, because there is no casualty, no emergency and no rescue anywhere in it: the film can state the ranking and then say, in the same breath and over the same footage, that this is not that, which is exactly what the digest requires of any film touching this material. This idea has been round once before. Its first version filmed a rescue crew drilling a response hundreds of times; that was dropped because the slate had already refused an emergency-services film, and because putting the texts' rarest readiness beside a real crew's trained capacity would have edged into presenting that capacity as a supernormal power — something the digest forbids a film to assert or to set out to debunk. The subject has moved to work in which the instant is real, the repetition is real, and nobody's life is at stake in either.

concept_links.why: The film is the digest's ordering of this material and nothing else from it. The refusal of wishing is narrated over the reading of the tree [C089-M:L25]; the goldsmith-and-potter image for making material workable is narrated over a chain being filed and a scarf being re-cut [C089-P4:L118]; the ladder of rarity and the claim that the hardest use of any of it is instant stillness for somebody else's sudden danger are narrated over the one moment in the film when nothing is happening at all, immediately after the fall, and are followed straight away by the film saying that this is not that [C089-P4:L98; C089-P4:L104–L108]; and the closing beat carries the digest's own deflation, that the powers are worldly, a support only, and not to be rested in [C089-P4:L26]. Every limit in the digest that bears on this film is honoured, and two of them are on screen. 'Meditation gives you superpowers' is refused by construction, because the film's whole subject is the last item on the list rather than the first three. 'Manifest your reality' is refused out loud. The miracle narratives are named once, as the opening of the source's own list, and are neither asserted as fact nor explained away. The divine eye is not filmed, not demonstrated and not offered as anything anyone in the frame has. Nobody's calm, endurance, skill or composure is presented as an attainment: the film says in as many words that nobody in the garden has anything the texts describe. Mind-reading is not recast as intuition, past-life recall is not recast as memory work, and no passage linking a person's circumstances to their past deeds is narrated or implied anywhere near real filmed people.

This is the concept that gives the film its proportion, and one statement of it is narrated at the exact moment the footage can carry it. The process the sources describe is almost entirely approach — settle, emerge, resolve, settle again, emerge — with three or four ordinary impulsions and then one single moment that is the knowledge itself [C101-P:L45–L48; C101-M:L5]; that is spoken over the last quarter hour of cutting and the fall. The graduated training, coarse before fine and near before far, and the requirement that a mind be taken through its states in every direction before anything is built on it, is spoken over the gang's plainest repetitions [C101-P:L87–L102]. The closing beat carries the digest's warning that the whole set is ranked below insight and is not to be rested in [C101-P4:L134]. Every limit in the digest is honoured and the sharpest one is a line of narration. The digest's requirement that a film neither assert nor set out to debunk that any real person has these abilities is met explicitly, in the fifth beat, about the people in the frame. The passages that correlate low birth, poverty and unpleasing appearance with past unwholesome deeds are not narrated, not paraphrased and not alluded to anywhere in the film [C101-P4:L58–L70]; nothing on screen is framed as anybody's desert; no household's garden, house, well or income is presented as a verdict on anybody. 'Trust your sixth sense' is refused, since the film's subject is repetition and method. Nothing is demonstrated on camera, and the apology passage is left alone.

C090 gives the film its opening and its ethical floor. The list of ten runs from the most dramatic claims to a craft, a treatment, a study, a ploughing and a sowing done right, which is narrated over the establishing aerial [C090-P4:L121–L127], and the definition underneath the whole list — the bringing about of what was intended — is narrated with it [C090-P4:L24]. The one item said to belong to fully freed people alone, an even response to the repulsive and to the alluring, is narrated over the unremarkable aftermath, and the digest's own correction is spoken with it: that this is balance reached through goodwill and not coldness, and that it is not visible on anybody's face in the frame [C090-P4:L85–L87; C090-M:L13]. The digest's most serious limit is stated out loud in the same beat: the protection stories must not become a promise that good people are kept safe, because that would mean anyone harmed lacked goodness. Prosperity is nowhere offered as virtue and poverty nowhere as fault; no garden, house or holding in the film is read as a measure of anybody, and the source's own honouring of a poor man's gift is the digest's reminder on that point [C090-P4:L431]. The power of resolve is cited only to say what it requires and what it is not [C090-P:L25–L46]. Charms and lore are not filmed, not endorsed and not mocked, and nothing in the film is presented as mind over matter.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That in this tradition the word translated as power means, at bottom, that what somebody intended actually came about, and that the sources' own list of it runs from miracles down to a trade done correctly. That the abilities at the top of the list are described as coming only after deep absorption and a long, graduated, repetitive training, and that the texts say plainly that wanting them achieves nothing. That the sources rank instant, invisible readiness for somebody else's danger above every spectacle, and that one kind of steadiness — meeting the repulsive and the alluring alike — is the only item they reserve for the fully freed. The felling is the last item on that list and the film says so; nobody in it is presented as having any of the others, and no claim is made or denied about anybody anywhere.
what_must_be_real: The gang's own job, on its own order, in its own time. No tree is felled for the film, no tree is chosen because it will look better falling, and no cut, rope, wedge or fall is repeated for a second take, because there is only one tree and one fall. Nothing about where people stand, how the rope is run, how the scarf is cut or when the saw comes out is arranged, suggested or delayed for the camera, and the crew stays where the gang puts it or does not film. If a tree hangs up, sits back on the saw, breaks a fence, or goes ten degrees off where it was cut to go, the film has that and keeps it. Nobody is named or followed as a character, nobody's skill is presented as an attainment or as foresight, and no one is asked to confirm any doctrine or to comment on it. The garden belongs to a household: that household decides what is filmed and what is not, and no house interior, name, gate number or income is put on screen. The felling licence and whatever permits the trade requires are the gang's and the owner's business and are not made a subject. No emergency, no injury and no near miss is filmed, staged, prolonged or implied for effect.
position_hint: middle to late in the group, and before the films about withdrawal and release: it resets what the group's remaining material is allowed to mean by power, from spectacle to method, and it is the only film in the group in which the decisive thing is over in two seconds. It also puts the group's hardest guard rail on screen early, by stating out loud that the film neither claims nor denies that anybody has what the texts describe. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Letting drilled, ordinary competence read as something supernormal, which is precisely the reading the digest forbids a film either to assert or to debunk.
Presenting anybody's steadiness, judgement or nerve as an attainment, or as evidence that the texts' ranking is being fulfilled in the frame.
Turning the fall into spectacle, so that the film's pleasure is destruction and the two seconds become a stunt rather than a proportion.

Romanticising dangerous work. A chainsaw, a rope and twenty metres of falling timber in a garden with a house in it are how people are actually killed, and nothing about how any of it is handled may be adjusted for a shot.
Letting a household's garden, house or circumstances read as a verdict on them, which is the divine-eye passage's shadow and the one thing the digest is most anxious about.
Implying that the gang is safe because it is careful, and so that anyone hurt in this trade was careless — the same cruelty as the protection stories turned into a promise.
Mourning the tree, so that the film becomes an argument about cutting rather than about a capacity discharging in an instant.
Filling the long approach with music or cutting it down, which would destroy the only thing the film has to show: the proportion between three hours and two seconds.
Letting the closing aerial of new light on cleared ground read as a reward, a release or an arrival.
drop_if: No gang and no garden owner will allow a whole felling to be filmed on their own terms, in their own order, with the crew kept where they put it.
The only fellings available inside the window are in open ground, so the constraint the film is built on — a tree with barely its own length to fall into — is absent.
The work cannot be filmed without someone standing where they would not otherwise stand, or without the gang changing how it does any part of it.
A household's house, name or circumstances cannot be kept off screen while the garden is filmed.
Height cannot be obtained over the gardens, so the two frames the film is built on — the crown above the canopy and the hole where it was — cannot be made.

connections.note: From a capacity that discharges in two seconds to one that has to be set up over a whole day before anybody can be out of reach.
Two films about the proportion between preparation and result, taken from opposite ends: here three hours for two seconds, there days of setting up for months of ordinary running.

selection.reason: It is the only film in the group in which a capacity built by years of repetition can be watched discharging completely in an instant, with no casualty, no emergency and nobody's heroism anywhere in it.

review.note: Rewritten and relocated 2026-09-24, off the rescue-crew subject entirely. The previous version filmed a rescue crew drilling a response hundreds of times; that is dropped because the slate has already refused an emergency-services film, and because setting the texts' rarest readiness beside a real crew's trained capacity would have edged into presenting that capacity as a supernormal power, which C101's digest forbids a film to assert or to set out to debunk. The concepts are unchanged and all three links are kept, re-grounded and rewritten. The subject is now a single garden felling in a crowded home-garden belt: three hours of reading, measuring and preparation, then about two seconds in which the whole of it arrives and nothing further can be corrected, with no casualty, no emergency, no rescue and nobody's heroism in the film. Every citation was re-tested against the three digests' own evidence before use, and the two off-by-one traps in this material were checked: C089-P4:L104–L108 and C090-P4:L85–L87 are the digest's own ranges, and C101-P:L45–L48 and C101-P:L87–L102 likewise. C101-P4:L58–L70, which correlates low birth, poverty and unpleasing appearance with past unwholesome deeds, is cited once in a concept link solely to record that it is refused, and is not narrated, paraphrased or alluded to anywhere in the film. C090's prohibition on 'good people are protected' is a spoken line in the sixth beat rather than a note in the file, and the fifth beat states in as many words that nobody in the frame has anything the texts describe and that the film is not out to prove or disprove it of anybody. Nobody's composure is presented as an attainment anywhere. The unconditioned is not reached for in this film at all: it belongs to the two films that follow, and nothing here is offered as a picture of it.

suggested_location.name: The home-garden timber belt of the Mirigama division, inland Gampaha, and the small sawmills on its lanes

also_known_as.name: gewatta
also_known_as.meaning: the home garden: a mixed, multi-storey stand of coconut, jak, mango, breadfruit, areca and timber trees around a house, which is where most of the island's sawn timber actually comes from
also_known_as.used_by: Sinhala usage throughout the wet zone

also_known_as.name: kos
also_known_as.meaning: jak, Artocarpus heterophyllus, one of the three species named as producing most of the timber volume that comes out of home gardens

also_known_as.name: kapana bime
also_known_as.meaning: loosely, the ground a tree is cut to fall into; the gap between a house, a well and a boundary that a felling has to be laid down inside. Reported as ordinary trade speech and not confirmed with anybody in the trade

suggested_location.region: Gampaha District, Western Province: the inland divisions of the district well behind the coast road, in the undulating wet-zone country of mixed home gardens, coconut and small sawmilling towns
suggested_location.why_here: Because the subject is ordinary and dense here rather than rare and remote. Gampaha holds about a fifth of the country's standing timber stock and, with the two districts beside it, the largest number of timber-based enterprises of anywhere on the island, and roughly seventy per cent of the industrial timber the country uses comes not from forest but from home gardens, coconut and rubber land and roadside and boundary trees. That means a felling gang here is not doing anything unusual: it is working through a list of gardens, and a crew can be attached to the list rather than to a set-up. It also means the constraint the film is built on is normal. These gardens are small and full, the houses are in among the trees, and a twenty-metre tree very often has barely its own length of opening to be laid into, between a tiled roof, a well, a shed and a service wire. That is what makes three hours of reading, measuring and rope work necessary, and what makes the two seconds at the end unrepeatable. The country is also quietly good from the air: an unbroken multi-storey canopy with roofs and lanes under it, one crown standing above the rest before the work, and a rectangle of new light on shaded ground afterwards. And there is no private grief anywhere in it, nobody is in danger, and no institution has to be persuaded to open anything — the film needs one gang, one garden owner and one small mill.
what_to_film: The canopy from height in the first and last hour, with the single crown standing clear above it, and the same frame again the following morning with the hole in it and the sun reaching the ground.

The reading of the tree at arm's length: the walk round the foot, the axe head tapped on a root buttress and the listening, the string and nut held up against the trunk, the crown studied from three positions.
The opening paced out, with everything at the edge of it in the same frame: the roof, the well head, the wall, the wire, the young coconut.
The plain repetitions, filmed without emphasis: the chain filed tooth by tooth on the tailgate, wedges split out of the last tree, a rope thrown over a limb on the third attempt.
A scarf cut and then checked with a flat hand laid inside it, close, because it is the one decision that cannot be revised.
The fall in a single unbroken shot from before the back-cut to after the dust, from a fixed position well outside the drop, and the long still moment that follows it.
The aftermath at working speed and in full: lopping, cross-cutting, the trunk rolled with a pole, chalk marks, the wet cut face, sawdust, the lorry loaded, somebody eating on the log.
Old stumps in other gardens, flat and grey, in the same light as the fresh one.
The small mill at the end of the day: the stack, the stickers between the boards, the yard of sawdust going dark.
suggested_location.access: By road inland from the coast and then on lanes and garden tracks. There is nothing restricted here and nothing institutional to open: the film needs the felling gang whose job it is, the household whose garden the tree stands in, and the mill the log goes to, and all three should be approached through people they already work with rather than cold. Felling and transport of timber are licensed, and the paperwork is the gang's and the owner's business rather than the film's subject; a crew should be sure its presence does not complicate it. The real hazards are the ordinary ones of the work and they are severe: a running saw, a rope under load, branches that come down separately, and a trunk that can sit back or roll. A crew has to be able to hold one fixed position well outside the drop for a whole morning without asking anybody to move, and to accept being sent further back. Drone flight over occupied home gardens needs the households' agreement whatever the general rules allow, and the lanes are close enough to houses that low flying is not appropriate. Nothing is felled in wind or heavy rain, so the schedule has to be able to absorb a wet week.
suggested_location.best_time: A dry spell, and a working week rather than a single day, taken against the gang's own list of gardens so that the film gets a tree that is genuinely coming down. Within the day, the canopy at either end and the fall whenever the cuts are finished. The following morning has to be held free for the gap and the new light, because the trunk will be gone by that afternoon. A second felling is worth planning for, since a tree that hangs up or goes off line is part of the subject and cannot be arranged.

suggested_location.research_note: Desk research only, and unverified on the ground. From the sources above: roughly seventy per cent of the industrial timber the country uses has to come from home gardens, coconut and rubber land, farm boundaries, roadsides and urban trees rather than from forest; jak, coconut and mango are named as three multi-purpose species together producing about thirty-eight per cent of the timber volume that comes out of home gardens; and over the last decade this district, with the two beside it, has held the largest number of timber-based enterprises in the country, with this district accounting for something on the order of a fifth of the national timber stock. The coordinates are the published position of a divisional secretariat in the district's inland country and are a direction towards the kind of ground the film needs, not a survey: no garden, tree, gang, household or mill has been identified, nobody has been approached, and no permission of any kind has been sought. Four things the film depends on are inferences about this district rather than confirmed facts: that small independent gangs still fell garden timber tree by tree here rather than the work being done by a mill's own crew, that a gang keeps a list a crew could be attached to inside a filming window, that a tree with barely its own length of opening is as common here as the density of the gardens suggests, and that height can be obtained over gardens with houses in them at all. The trade speech recorded above under the local names is reported and not confirmed. No photograph of this district's gardens, of a felling, of a gang or of a mill was found on Wikimedia Commons; the one image is of the tree species, photographed in another district.

unknowns: Whether independent felling gangs still take garden timber tree by tree in this district, or whether the work has moved to mills' own crews with machines that would change the whole shape of the morning.
Whether a gang's own list of gardens can be made to meet a filming window, and whether it will take a crew along on it rather than offering a demonstration.
Whether a tree with barely its own length of opening — the constraint the film is built on — can be found inside the window, or whether the available fellings are all in open ground.
Whether the fall can be filmed in one unbroken shot from a position the gang considers safe, and whether that position gives the frame the film needs.
Whether height can be obtained over occupied home gardens here, and whether the single crown above the canopy and the hole afterwards read from the air as strongly as they appear to from the ground.
Whether a household will allow its garden to be filmed while its house, name and circumstances are kept off screen.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. The location is proposed by Claude from desk research and is unverified. No scene or shot is decided here.
